newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks little changed in London, Dow seen up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks little changed in London, Dow seen up.

text.p: U.S. stocks were steady in London in light and quiet trading after the recent volatility on Wall Street.
"There really are few features. The market is just quietly restrained," said one London broker.
He said he expected Wall Street to open higher initially after yesterday's strong rebound, "but after that, it's anybody's guess," he added.
The Dow finished 19.75 points lower at 6422.94 after initially shedding 75 points on Wednesday.
Traders said the renewed buying signalled the end to the two-day sell-off.

Technical analyst Robin Griffiths of HSBC James Capel said he expected the bull market to continue, with the Dow topping 7,000 before the rally is exhausted. "Right from the start, this bull has looked like doubling, so the Dow Jones has 7,200 written all over it," he said in a recent report.
At 1158 GMT, the December S&P future contract was up 0.80 points to 748.45 on Globex. The December long bond futures contract was up 7/32 to 115-29-32.
Dealers said a positive outlook from Hewlett Packard executives late on Wednesday helped push the stock up $3/8 to $56-1/8 in London, after the $1-1/4 rise in New York yesterday.
"Other than that, there doesn't seem to be much interest," the dealer said.
